Arash Heidari et al.29 recommended the hybrid optimization algorithm and density correlation degree for a 
reliable method for data aggregation on the industrial IoT. An approach for building optimum spanning trees 
using a combination of genetic operators, artificial bee colonies, and density correlation degree is proposed 
in this work. This method calculates the trees’ fitness by taking their mobility probabilities, residual energy, 
and hop count distances from the base station. The simulations show that the proposed algorithm outperforms 
well-established approaches regarding data collection reliability, particularly when compared to IIoT’s Reliable 
Spanning Tree (RST) building algorithm and the HCD-based construction algorithm. The suggested approach 
improves dependability over a wide range of node counts by considering distance, energy consumption, 
displacement likelihood, and reliability.
Arash Heidari et al. 30 discussed the Blockchain and Radial Basis Function Neural Networks (RBFNN) for 
the Internet of Drones (IoD) in a Secure Intrusion Detection Platform. The suggested approach may enhance 
data integrity and storage to facilitate intelligent decision-making across several IoDs. The author discusses a 
paradigm for building decentralized predictive analytics and a blockchain for efficiently applying and distributing 
DL approaches. The author tested the model with many datasets to prove the practicality and efficiency of using 
the blockchain-based DL method in IoD settings. According to the results, the proposed model is a great choice 
for creating classifiers that comply with the requirements of network intrusion detection. The suggested model 
can beat the state-of-the-art specificity, F1, recall, precision, and accuracy approaches.
Arash Heidari et al.31 deliberated on the reliability and availability of wireless sensor networks in industrial 
applications by considering permanent faults. The reliability and availability of WSNs with long-term problems 
are examined in this research. Using fault trees and Markov chain analysis, the proposed technique evaluates a 
network’s performance under different failure scenarios. Using these technologies, the author may discover and 
analyze potential failure situations and their projected impacts on the network’s dependability. In addition to 
revealing WSNs’ serious shortcomings, the data provide helpful recommendations for improving the systems’ 
performance. The results demonstrate that these assessment techniques have the potential to significantly 
improve fault handling, decrease damage risk, and enable WSN developers to make informed decisions.
Zahra Amiri et al.32 introduced nature-inspired algorithms in the IoT-based healthcare service. A Systematic 
Literature Review (SLR) is the previously settled approach for conducting thorough investigations into relevant 
studies. The author uses crucial criterion-based painstaking categorization to categorize these algorithms into 
genetic algorithms, ant colony optimization, cuckoo algorithms, hybrid techniques, particle swarm optimization, 
and other ways. With a share of 37.9% of instances, MATLAB stands out as the most popular programming 
language among researchers. The most important factor in our assessment, which accounts for 18.4% of the 
total, is flexibility.
Kouros Zanbouri et al. 33 presented the Glowworm Swarm Optimization (GSO) for a multi-objective 
technique for performance optimization of blockchain-based industrial IoT. The GSO algorithm provides a 
novel way to reconcile these competing goals, drawing inspiration from the cooperative genius of glowworms 
in nature. In light of the competing goals of blockchain technology, this article suggests a novel way to optimize 
the performance of blockchain-based IIoT using the GSO algorithm. The suggested IIoT system uses the GSO 
algorithm to adapt to network needs and effectively manage node interactions to overcome the usual scalability 
issues with blockchain technology. The GSO algorithm minimizes inefficiencies and bottlenecks via optimal 
resource allocation and decision-making.
Arash Heidari et al. 34 offered ChatGPT’s Components, capabilities, applications, and opportunities. The 
author delves into ChatGPT’s inner workings, limitations, possible uses, and prospects within open-domain 
conversations. After defining chatbots, the author goes on to describe ChatGPT’s components. The author 
proposes a new taxonomy for their classification. Four types of chatbots are included in this taxonomy: rule-
based, retrieval-based, generative, and hybrid. The author will now go over the features and limitations of 
ChatGPT. The author concludes by outlining future research prospects and possible ChatGPT uses. According 
to the findings, the transformer-based chatbot model known as ChatGPT uses encoders to generate coherent 
answers.
Zahra Amiri et al. 35 suggested AI techniques and strategies for climate change mitigation. This research 
uncovered new information on the dependability and efficacy of DL approaches for dealing with climate change 
issues. The six main categories into which we categorized climate change ML approaches are ecosystems, 
industry, buildings and cities, transportation, agriculture, and hybrid applications. Subsequently, cutting-edge 
studies on ML methods and their uses in addressing climate change mitigation concerns have been emphasized. 
Furthermore, many challenges and concerns aboutusing ML in the context of climate change have been 
identified, which is expected to encourage further study into mitigating the catastrophic future consequences 
of climate change. According to the data, most articles (38.5 percent) used Python as their simulation platform.
Mehdi Asadi et al.36 proposed a comprehensive Survey on Evolving Threats and Defense Strategies. The study 
assesses how botnets avoid detection and potential countermeasures by examining previous studies and giving a 
thorough introduction to botnets, including their history, current strategies, and evasion methods. By shedding 
light on evasion and detection techniques, it aims to educate the research community about botnets and the 
difficulties in fighting them. It also provides advice on how to handle security problems properly. The survey’s 
last section covers strategies to enhance botnets, detection via encryption and covert channels, and other such 
topics, which outline suggestions for further study. The goal is to help researchers tackle botnets more effectively 
by guiding the development of stronger security solutions.

resposta.resumo: O trecho apresenta uma revisão de literatura que destaca a superação de obstáculos ao uso de deep learning em áreas como saúde e bioinformática, e descreve múltiplos estudos que combinam algoritmos bio‑inspirados, blockchain e redes neurais para otimizar coleta de dados, detecção de intrusões, confiabilidade de sensores e desempenho de IIoT. São citados critérios de avaliação (escalabilidade, flexibilidade, latência, métricas de classificação) e diversas propostas que melhoram confiabilidade, eficiência e segurança em ambientes distribuídos.

Aplicar criptografia baseada em atributos (ABE) para controle de acesso granular aos dados registrados no blockchain.
Explorar aprendizado federado combinado com DNNs‑BCT para melhorar a escalabilidade e privacidade em ambientes de edge computing.
Avaliar a abordagem em cenários de cidades inteligentes com múltiplas organizações públicas e privadas, medindo interoperabilidade e latência.
Incorporar algoritmos de otimização bio‑inspirados (ex.: GSO, algoritmos genéticos) para ajustar parâmetros de consenso blockchain e reduzir consumo energético.
Estender a análise de confiabilidade usando árvores de falha e cadeias de Markov para suportar revogação de credenciais em tempo real.

resposta.interpretacao: O trabalho se insere em uma tendência crescente de combinar deep learning e blockchain para melhorar a detecção de anomalias em IoT, adotando métricas de desempenho padrão da literatura (escalabilidade, latência, precisão). Os estudos citados reforçam a necessidade de soluções que conciliem segurança, confiabilidade e eficiência energética, apontando caminhos para aprimorar a proposta DNNs‑BCT.
